neutral_facts.value: The accused, along with his father and brother, went to the house of the deceased with weapons. They had a verbal altercation and started beating the son of the deceased. When the deceased intervened, the brother of the accused, upon exhortation from his father, fired at the deceased, resulting in his death. The prosecution witnesses provided detailed accounts of the incident, including the use of weapons, the beating of the deceased's family members, and the subsequent shooting of the deceased. The trial court convicted all three accused under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC, and the High Court upheld this conviction.

value.trial_court: Conviction under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC

quotes.text: The trial court convicted all the three accused under section 302 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The High Court observed that all the accused persons went to the house of the deceased Bhagirath with the intention to teach him a lesson.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant, along with his father and brother, went to the house of the deceased with weapons, engaged in a verbal altercation, and that the brother of the appellant, on exhortation of his father, fired at the deceased, resulting in his death. The prosecution contended that the appellant was rightly convicted under sections 302 and 34 of the IPC due to the prearranged plan and common intention among the accused.

quotes.text: The prosecution case was that the appellant went to the house of the deceased along with his father and his brother. The father of the appellant asked the deceased to reap their crop. The deceased informed him that he was busy and could not reap their crop. On hearing this, the father of the appellant got very annoyed. The next day, all the three again went to the house of the deceased. The appellant and his father were armed with lathis and his brother with a firearm. They insisted that the deceased should reap their crop. On getting a negative response, the appellant and his father started abusing and beating the son of the deceased. The family members of the deceased tried to intervene and in the process they also got injured. The deceased tried to save his son. At that point of time, father of the appellant exhorted the other son to shoot the deceased, who then shot at the deceased in the stomach, which resulted in his death.

defence_argument.value: The appellant contended that in the facts and circumstances of the case, Section 34 IPC could not be invoked, arguing that there was no direct evidence of a common intention or prearranged plan among the accused.

quotes.text: In the instant appeal, the appellant contended that in the facts and circumstances of the case Section 34 IPC could not be invoked.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle of vicarious or constructive liability under Section 34 IPC, emphasizing the need for a common intention and actual participation in the commission of the crime, which may develop on the spot but must be anterior in point of time to the commission of the crime.

quotes.text: A person can be vicariously responsible for the acts of others, if he had a common intention to commit the offence. The vicarious or constructive liability under Section 34 IPC can arise only when two conditions stand fulfilled, i.e., the mental element or the intention to commit the criminal act conjointly with others; and the actual participation in one form or the other in the commission of the crime.
